clue.text: Aggressive delivery man outside door …

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a short-pitched ball that rears up at the batsman's head
a doorman who keeps order at a nightclub entrance

explanation.surface: A menacing courier lurking outside someone's front door, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 5-across for a cricket-flavoured surface; it has no role in the wordplay. Cricket is a bat-and-ball game where the bowler delivers the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a fast short cricket ball and a nightclub doorman share the one name.

clue.text: Rotten type given breakfast for soldiers?

definitions.meaning: soldiers are strips of toast dipped in a boiled egg; a spoiled egg would be a poor breakfast for them

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a worthless person, and literally names a spoiled egg to serve with toast fingers.

clue.text: Apprehension caused by universal joints, we hear

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal

indicators.note: we hear means the word is heard spoken, not spelled

parts.note: knees are joints of the leg

explanation.surface: Anxiety brought on by aching joints, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: U plus a word sounding like KNEES gives the answer, the K being silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is a feeling of worry or anxiety, the same as apprehension.

clue.text: Company millions guarantee settlement

parts.note: a promise is a guarantee

explanation.surface: A firm guarantees a multi-million payout in a legal settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is an agreement reached by each side conceding something.

clue.text: Element of difficulty in the Navy

indicators.note: in means the difficulty sits inside the navy abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
ado means fuss or trouble, as in without further ado

explanation.surface: A spot of trouble in the Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: … delivering starters of black or white fish

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the three words that follow

parts.note: the ling is an edible sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Continuing 1-across: a menacing deliveryman bringing round black or white fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowling is the act of delivering the ball to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling is the cricket term for propelling the ball, so the present participle matches the activity.

clue.text: Sailor turned up with new Maltese 19, for example

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A sailor appearing with a new Maltese, as though about a crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is COPPER, the answer to 19-down, an example of a non-precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a common metal that corrodes, unlike gold or silver, so it is an example.

clue.text: Stop doctor and answer

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC science-fiction time traveller

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt both the doctor and the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a command to a horse to halt, so it means stop.

clue.text: Popular actors must see injustice

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Equity is the actors' trade union

explanation.surface: Popular performers have to witness unfairness.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the trade union for British actors and performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequity means unfairness, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Develops land within the boundaries of Gleneagles

indicators.note: within means the land goes inside the boundary letters
the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an estate is a large area of land

explanation.surface: Developing land inside the grounds of Gleneagles, a famous Scottish golf resort.
explanation.definitionFit: To gestate is to carry and grow, used figuratively for an idea that develops.

clue.text: Unattainable ambition of armed criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongdoing, so these letters are set to a corrupt new order

explanation.surface: A gunman's impossible hope of a big score.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a hope that will never be realised, so the word fits an unreachable goal.

clue.text: Learns one's insurance must be held in case of disasters

indicators.note: held in means the following pieces are enclosed by the outer letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I plus the S of the contraction
insurance is cover against loss

explanation.surface: Someone finding out their policy only applies in case of catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disasters' looks like part of the surface's insurance story, but only its outside letters are used, with 'held in' signalling that they wrap around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to find out, a close synonym of learning something new.

clue.text: Science attached to golf and food appreciation

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
astronomy is the science of stars and planets

explanation.surface: A study tacked on to golf and fine dining, like a country-club curriculum.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomy is the art of choosing, cooking and enjoying good eating.

clue.text: Island origin of Cambridge university graduate

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Asking where a Cambridge graduate originally came from, as though the answer were an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island of the Caribbean, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Psychic working at Delphi etc. with no daughter

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a fresh order
with no means the daughter is taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: A seer at work at Delphi, home of the ancient Greek oracle, without her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from the letters of 'at Delphi etc.' and 'working' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepathic person reads minds, the gift a psychic claims.

clue.text: Met the pariah upset in the Coliseum, for example

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: An outcast meets someone who is upset at the Roman Colosseum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum in Rome is the most famous example of an open oval arena for spectacles.

clue.text: Impression created by bay?

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse, so the mark it leaves on the ground is its foot's imprint

explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests a stretch of coast, but here it is a horse of that colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's foot pressed into soft ground leaves the shape of its hoof.

clue.text: Provides cover for house, coming in fourth at Chester

indicators.note: coming in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A horse finishing fourth in a race at Chester, a racecourse town, while a house gets covered.
explanation.definitionFit: To thatch is to roof a building with straw or reeds.

clue.text: Good free press network

parts.note: to rid is to free
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A good free newspaper network.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is a grid of parallel bars, a network of lines.

clue.text: Part of road that's difficult to bear?

parts.note: hard means difficult
to shoulder a burden is to bear it

explanation.surface: A stretch of highway that is a burden to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: The hard shoulder is the British name for the emergency lane at the edge of a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The paved strip beside a motorway carriageway is a section of the road used only in emergencies.

clue.text: Bobby and Penny?

definitions.meaning: a bobby is a British police officer, slang named after Sir Robert Peel
a penny is a small coin made of the reddish metal

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a penny is only an example of a small brown coin of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A British policeman and a low-value coin both carry this slang name.

clue.text: English type needing to accept Conservative lead

indicators.note: to accept means the type takes the Conservative inside

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: An English sort of person needing to back the Conservative leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to guide or conduct them, a verbal sense of lead.

clue.text: Sizeable order

explanation.definitionFit: Tidy means both fairly large, as in a substantial sum, and neat or arranged as a verb.

clue.text: People looking on as Prescott dances

indicators.note: dances means the letters jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: Onlookers watch a politician dance, John Prescott having been Britain's deputy prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators are an audience, those who watch an event without taking part.

clue.text: Track bag found outside hotel

indicators.note: found outside means the bag wraps around the hotel letter

parts.note: a case is a piece of luggage
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Tracking down a bag left outside a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to pursue or follow, the same as to track a quarry.

clue.text: Wrap hamper

definitions.meaning: thin metal sheet used to cover food

explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen sheet metal wraps food, and to thwart a plan is to hinder it.

clue.text: Mostly difficult slang name reported for instrument

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: reported means the following word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: moniker is an informal word for a name

explanation.surface: Someone struggling with a tricky nickname that has been passed on for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims HARD to HAR; 'reported' gives MONICA, which sounds like MONIKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is a reed instrument played by blowing, an example of the class.

clue.text: Animal — one very quiet in house

indicators.note: in means the pieces before it sit inside the house abbreviation

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: An animal that sits very quietly at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus, shortened colloquially, is a large African mammal.

clue.text: Top room for one troll with no bread

parts.note: a single is a hotel room for one guest

indicators.note: with no means the following item is removed

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Accommodation upstairs for a lone troll who has no bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes ROLL out of TROLL, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, a garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Runs into bar for a bit of work

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone dashing into a pub for a little job.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a longer piece of writing or music.
